title: CuTe Layout Algebra for GPU Kernel Development
key_concepts: Hierarchical layout algebra for memory mapping
critical_patterns: Row-Major: Sequential row access, good for C/C++
Column-Major: Sequential column access, good for Fortran/BLAS
Swizzled Layout: Avoids bank conflicts in shared memory
Blocked/Tiled Layout: Enhances cache efficiency and GPU thread mapping
constraints: Ensure proper stride to avoid bank conflicts
Match layout with memory order (e.g., PyTorch row-major)
Consider alignment requirements for tensor cores
Layouts must be architecture-specific for optimal performance
compressed_summary: CuTe Layout Algebra provides a robust framework for defining how data maps to memory in GPU kernels. It abstracts address calculations through composable layouts, which consist of shapes (logical dimensions) and strides (memory traversal steps). This abstraction reduces bugs, enhances compile-time optimizations, and ensures architecture portability. Key patterns include row-major and column-major layouts, with swizzled and blocked layouts addressing specific performance needs like bank conflict avoidance and cache efficiency. Practical usage involves creating tensors with layouts, partitioning layouts for thread blocks, and ensuring alignment for tensor cores. Constraints include avoiding bank conflicts through proper stride selection, aligning layouts with memory order (e.g., PyTorch's row-major), and adhering to architecture-specific requirements. Advanced operations like layout composition and logical division enable complex memory patterns. Overall, CuTe's layout algebra is essential for efficient GPU kernel development, providing automatic address calculation, optimization opportunities, and control over memory coalescing.
